gloss: in heaps; in abundance; a whole lot

definitions.gloss: in heaps; in abundance; a whole lot; piles of
definitions.explanation: Describes a large quantity or amount of something, often with a visual image of things being piled up or accumulated.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}がどっさり{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: A huge pile of packages arrived.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}をどっさり{買|か}ってきた。
examples.english: I bought a whole lot of vegetables.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}から{帰|かえ}ると、{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}に{書類|しょるい}がどっさり{積|つ}まれていた。
examples.english: When I returned from my trip, documents were piled up in heaps on my desk.

notes:
A mimetic adverb expressing a large quantity of something, often with the connotation of being physically heaped or piled up. Conveys the impression of an overwhelming or surprising amount.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- どっさり{届|とど}く: to arrive in large quantities
- どっさり{積|つ}む: to pile up in heaps
- どっさり{買|か}う: to buy a whole lot
- {仕事|しごと}がどっさり: heaps of work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たっぷり: plenty, generously — emphasizes sufficiency, often positive
- たくさん: a lot, many — the standard neutral word for large quantity
- がっぽり: in large amounts — typically for money or profits
- ごっそり: the whole lot — implies taking everything at once

REGISTER:
Informal and colloquial. Often used in spoken Japanese to emphasize quantity with a vivid, slightly exaggerated tone.
